idea: Week three, from the story bank: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: Madhya Pradesh produced 3.7 million tonnes of spices in 2023-24, 29.8% of India's 12.5 million tonnes and the highest of 31 states and UTs. Gujarat (1.4 million) and Andhra Pradesh (1.3 million) came next. It led in each year from 2020-21 to 2023-24, by at least twice the next state.

The count is by weight and follows the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices Development's list, which includes garlic and ginger. State totals, not per person. Figures given by the Commerce Ministry in a Lok Sabha answer of 29 July 2025.
source: Directorate of Arecanut and Spices Development (DASD), Calicut, as given by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce), Government of India, in its reply to Lok Sabha Unstarred Question No. 1570 of 29 July 2025 (Export of Spices from India), Annexure-I: state-wise and year-wise production of spices, 2020-21 to 2024-25, in '000 tonnes. The 2023-24 and 2022-23 columns are used; the 2024-25 column is marked as a second advance estimate and is not used, because the Spices Board's own table (Major Spice/state wise area and production of spices, 2021-22 to 2025-26) now shows 2024-25 as final with a different grand total (12,991.893 thousand tonnes, against 12,369.981 here). 31 state and UT rows (Jharkhand is typed in from the answer text because the table reader drops it); the 2023-24 rows add up to the printed all-India row (12,483.787), which agrees with the Spices Board grand total for 2023-24 (12,483.215). The Spices Board table lists garlic and ginger among the major spices, which is why the screen says they are in the list. State totals, not per-person figures.
question: Which spice can't you cook without?
